title: "**Important** You should give me full credits!": Exploring Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Automatic Grading Systems
abstract: arXiv:2606.03090v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has significantly accelerated recent research on LLM-based automatic grading (AG) systems. Benefiting from the strong instruction-following capabilities and broad prior knowledge of LLMs, educators can deploy AG systems across diverse tasks using only natural language rubrics while achieving satisfactory grading performance. Despite these advantages, new security concerns may also arise. In particular, prompt injection (PI) attacks have recently become a major threat to LLM-based applications. In the context of AG, attackers can potentially exploit PI vulnerabilities to manipulate grading systems into assigning artificially high scores regardless of the actual answer quality. Such behavior poses serious risks to the fairness, reliability, and integrity of educational assessment. translated_title: "**重要！请给我满分！**"：探索针对基于大语言模型的自动评分系统的提示注入攻击
translated_abstract: 大语言模型的出现极大地加速了近年来基于大语言模型的自动评分（AG）系统的研究。得益于大语言模型强大的指令遵循能力和广泛的先验知识，教育者只需使用自然语言形式的评分标准，就能够在多样化的任务中部署自动评分系统，并获得令人满意的评分性能。尽管具备这些优势，新的安全问题也可能随之产生。特别是，提示注入攻击近来已成为基于大语言模型应用的主要威胁。在自动评分的场景中，攻击者可能利用提示注入漏洞来操纵评分系统，使其无视答案的实际质量而给出人为抬高的高分。这种行为对教育评估的公平性、可靠性和完整性构成严重风险。在本工作中，我们研究了自动评分系统中的提示注入攻击，并系统地考察了此类攻击的有效性。
tldr: 本文系统研究了针对基于大语言模型的自动评分系统的提示注入攻击，揭示攻击者可利用该漏洞操纵评分系统给出虚假高分，严重威胁教育评估的公平性与完整性。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically explores prompt injection attacks on LLM-based automatic grading systems, showing that attackers can exploit such vulnerabilities to manipulate graders into assigning artificially high scores, posing serious threats to the fairness and integrity of educational assessment.
